A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLPF research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original repeated path-construction experiments, training and testing results, PCA/SVD analyses, and generalization experiments in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds layer-mean measurements, additional model–dataset experiments, and a stricter loss-threshold experiment.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same Move, VarianceCorrection, Train, and AngleConformal operations and formulas. Corrected training-step comments and newly documented CIFAR architecture details do not establish changes to the proposed method; additional architectures are evaluation configurations.

E1.justification: v2 Figure 8 extends model-to-model path construction to CIFAR100, which v1 used only for model-to-origin experiments. All four datasets already appear in v1. MobileNet and ShuffleNet add model configurations rather than new data domains.

E2.justification: AutoNEB remains the comparison method discussed in Section 4. v2 adds a literature-attributed numerical loss comparison with it, but introduces no additional competing path-finding method. MobileNet and ShuffleNet are architectures tested with LLPF, not competing algorithms.

E3.justification: v2 adds MobileNet/ShuffleNet configurations and an alternative ResNet18/CIFAR10 protocol targeting loss below 0.006: Table 6 specifies batch size 128, 8,000 path iterations, and refinement until loss ≤0.005 or r>20,000. Section 4 also adds final test-loss agreement with initial test loss as a validity criterion. Original numerical settings in Tables 1–3 are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds two targeted checks: empirical examination of the zero-mean approximation across 100 ResNet18 models (Appendix A.2/Figure 7), and construction of a path under a stricter 0.006 loss threshold (A.7/Figure 10). Existing variance, PCA, and dimensionality analyses remain.

E5.justification: Figure 8 newly specifies only one repetition per additional experiment because of computational constraints. The retained main experiments still report 200/40/10 repetitions, means with standard-deviation bands, and moving-average smoothing. No increase in their run counts is reported.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands results with three additional model–dataset path trajectories, the 0.006-threshold path, and layer-mean measurements (Figures 7, 8, and 10). Figure 2's CCT7 curves also change; its final mean test loss rises from approximately 0.50 to 0.53 without an explanation of the revision. Figure 5's reported ImageNet accuracy example, 69.758% to 70.55%, is retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the low-loss-space and variance-sphere definitions, and the near-zero-mean approximation remain unchanged. The Equation 6 proof moves from v1 Appendix A.2 to v2 A.3 without substantive revision. The new mean-weight plot supplies empirical evidence, not a new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the connectivity, parameter-redundancy, visualization, and generalization claims. The introduction newly claims lower maximum path loss than prior AutoNEB work and stronger quantitative support for connectedness.

C2.justification: v2 adds a hypothesis that nearby local minima trap paths starting from sharp minima, and explains the tradeoff between path quality and computation through step sizes and training rounds. It interprets the stricter-threshold result as stronger connectivity evidence and softens the ResNet18 high-frequency observation from absent to less pronounced.

D1.justification: Tables 4–5 newly document preprocessing, augmentation, GPUs, and execution times. v2 also specifies stopping-loss smoothing, whole-test-set evaluation, the CIFAR ResNet18 convolutional stem, and implementation sources. These are disclosures rather than established changes to retained experiments. Table 6 documents the new threshold experiment, although Figure 8 hyperparameters are deferred to source code outside the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for MNIST, CIFAR, ImageNet, MobileNetV2, ShuffleNetV2, and model implementations. It strengthens its positioning against AutoNEB through the lower-loss claim, while retaining the existing singular-learning and mode-connectivity background.

P1.justification: Several definition, algorithm-explanation, evaluation, and dimensionality paragraphs are shortened or rewritten, with additional hyperparameter explanations. The six-section main narrative remains intact; appendix subsections are expanded and renumbered while retaining the original proof, PCA analysis, and hyperparameter material.

P2.justification: The appendix gains dedicated layer-mean, additional-model, and stricter-threshold plots, together with preprocessing, runtime, and alternative-setting tables. Existing plots receive sizing, axis-notation, and spacing adjustments. The unchanged ResNet18 PCA visualization moves from Figure 7 to Figure 9; it is not removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through substantial implementation documentation and adds useful checks of the zero-mean approximation and stricter low-loss paths. These gains are limited by one-repetition additional experiments and missing Figure 8 hyperparameters. Its stronger AutoNEB claim compares ResNet18 with a cited ResNet20 result, so it does not establish superiority under matching settings. The core algorithms and theoretical arguments remain unchanged.
